content.title: What are Operators and Type Casting?
content.description: Operators perform operations on variables and values, while type casting converts a value from one data type to another.

content.content: Java provides a rich set of operators for performing arithmetic, comparison, logical, assignment, and bitwise operations. Sometimes, values need to be converted between different data types. This process is known as type casting.

content.title: Why Learn Operators?
content.content: Operators form the foundation of programming because almost every calculation, comparison, and decision depends on them.
Types of Operators
Java groups operators into several categories based on the type of operation they perform.

items.question: Arithmetic Operators
items.answer: Used for mathematical calculations like +, -, *, /, and %.

items.question: Relational Operators
items.answer: Used to compare values such as ==, !=, >, <, >=, and <=.

items.question: Logical Operators
items.answer: Used to combine conditions using &&, ||, and !.

items.question: Assignment Operators
items.answer: Used to assign values, such as =, +=, -=, *=, and /=.

content.content: Relational Operators
Relational operators compare two values and always return a boolean result.

content.title: Remember
content.content: Relational operators always produce either true or false.
Logical Operators
Logical operators combine multiple conditions and are commonly used inside decision-making statements like if and while.

content.title: Logical Operators Example

content.content: Assignment Operators
Assignment operators assign values to variables and can perform operations while assigning.
Unary Operators
Unary operators operate on a single operand. The increment (++) and decrement (--) operators are frequently used in loops.

content.title: Increment & Decrement

content.content: Type Casting
Type casting converts one data type into another. Java supports two types of casting: implicit (widening) and explicit (narrowing).

items.question: Implicit (Widening) Casting
items.answer: Automatically converts a smaller data type into a larger data type.

items.question: Explicit (Narrowing) Casting
items.answer: Requires manual conversion because data may be lost.

content.content: Real-Life Analogy

content.title: Using Different Measuring Cups
content.content: Imagine pouring water from a small cup into a larger container—it fits easily (implicit casting). Pouring from a large container into a small cup may lose some water (explicit casting).

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Interviewers frequently ask about operator precedence, increment operators, implicit vs explicit casting, and integer division.
Common Mistakes

items.question: Why does 10 / 3 return 3 instead of 3.33?
items.answer: Because both operands are integers, resulting in integer division.

items.question: Why is data lost during explicit casting?
items.answer: Because a larger data type is converted into a smaller one.

items.question: What is a common mistake with == ?
items.answer: Using == to compare String objects instead of using the equals() method.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Use implicit casting whenever possible. Use explicit casting only when necessary and be aware of possible data loss.
